resolutions.title: The apply-later-than-L branch runs an 'ordinary single' that the engine counts as the open pair's member, so a non-blind pair covers the invoked slot
resolutions.action: applied the ratified A′: with openPair standing and an apply later than L the run is the pair's missing member — its REVIEWED COMMIT is the first parent of the commit that added the landed member, the external saves under its own T0 token, a fresh re-run is briefed with that commit; only a stale member (no openPair) makes the run a single, with the supersession notice

options_presented.label: A
options_presented.body: Body: with openPair standing and an apply later than L, do not run a single. Say the pair is superseded and run a NEW pair (/orbit:review --as <mode> --reviewer blind-pair <change>). Its launch opens a later membership window, so the old landed member stays in the old pair and the new halves form a blind pair on the current state. Re-word the scenario 'A re-run after an apply is a single' and its test to match, and assert the gate after the run.

options_presented.label: B
options_presented.body: Engine: an apply later than a launch ENDS that launch's pair, so later passes read as singles. This changes rc17a's membership requirement, a stated non-goal here, and would mean a scope call and probably a split.

options_presented.label: C
options_presented.body: Keep the branch and state the outcome in the named limit of 'A pair's external half reads the pair's reviewed state': after an apply later than L, the next half completes the old pair non-blind and the gate counts it blind. Drop the word 'single' wherever it describes this run.
